title: Career Roadmap: Junior Data Scientist
summary: A Junior Data Scientist uses statistics, programming, data analysis, and machine learning to uncover patterns, answer business questions, and develop data-driven predictions. The role combines analytical thinking with the ability to explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical teams.

blocks.text: A Junior Data Scientist uses statistics, programming, data analysis, and machine learning to uncover patterns, answer business questions, and develop data-driven predictions. The role combines analytical thinking with the ability to explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical teams.
A B.Sc in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence provides a relevant foundation in programming, mathematics, statistics, databases, and machine learning.
Typical career directions include:

blocks.label: Data Science
blocks.text: Build predictive models and conduct statistical analysis.

blocks.label: Machine Learning
blocks.text: Train, evaluate, and improve models for practical tasks.

blocks.label: Business Analytics
blocks.text: Convert data into business insights and recommendations.

blocks.label: Applied AI
blocks.text: Develop data-driven AI features and intelligent applications.

blocks.label: Product Analytics
blocks.text: Study user behaviour, engagement, retention, and conversion.

sections.heading: What does a Junior Data Scientist do?

items.text: Collect data from databases, files, APIs, and business systems.
Clean datasets, handle missing values, and investigate inconsistencies.
Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) to discover patterns and relationships.
Apply statistics to understand distributions, correlations, and uncertainty.
Build and evaluate machine-learning models for prediction or classification.
Compare model performance against suitable baselines and evaluation metrics.
Create charts, dashboards, and reports to communicate findings.
Collaborate with data engineers, analysts, software developers, and business teams.
Document experiments, assumptions, limitations, and reproducible workflows.

blocks.text: A junior data scientist is not expected to know every advanced AI technique. Employers typically value strong fundamentals, practical projects, sound evaluation, and the ability to explain the reasoning behind an analysis.

rows.text: Python, functions, OOP basics, data structures
NumPy, pandas, data cleaning, joins, missing values
Joins, subqueries, CTEs, aggregations, window functions
Cross-validation, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, RMSE

Data storytelling, technical reports, presenting insights

Clean, transform, explore, and analyse structured data.
pandas documentation · NumPy documentation

Optional tools to learn later include XGBoost, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, cloud data services, and deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow. Choose these based on the projects and roles you target.
Year 1
Programming and mathematics

items.text: Learn Python fundamentals and problem-solving.
Study probability, statistics, linear algebra, and calculus basics.
Practise SQL queries and relational database concepts.
Learn Git, Jupyter, NumPy, and pandas.
Complete small projects involving data cleaning and visualisation.

blocks.text: Year 2
Data analysis and statistical reasoning

items.text: Perform EDA on real-world datasets.
Learn hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and regression.
Build visual reports using Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Power BI.
Practise SQL joins, CTEs, and window functions.
Publish two well-documented analysis projects on GitHub.

blocks.text: Year 3
Machine learning and specialisation

items.text: Learn regression, classification, clustering, and feature engineering.
Use cross-validation and appropriate evaluation metrics.
Study data leakage, overfitting, class imbalance, and model interpretability.
Build an end-to-end machine-learning project.
Seek internships in data science, analytics, or machine learning.

blocks.text: Year 4
Deployment and job readiness

items.text: Complete a capstone solving a clearly defined problem.
Deploy a model using a lightweight app or API.
Learn reproducibility, testing, documentation, and basic deployment.
Practise SQL, Python, statistics, and ML interview questions.
Apply for Junior Data Scientist, Data Analyst, and ML Trainee roles.

blocks.text: If you are already in your final year, focus on three strong projects, SQL and statistics revision, model evaluation, GitHub documentation, and a simple deployed demonstration rather than trying to learn every AI framework.
Project 1 — Exploratory Data Analysis
Beginner
Analyse a public retail, student performance, or public health dataset. Clean the data, investigate patterns, visualise findings, and write five evidence-based insights.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Python, pandas, statistics, data visualisation.
Project 2 — Customer Churn Prediction
Intermediate
Train a model to estimate which customers may leave a service. Compare a baseline with more complex models, evaluate precision and recall, and explain the business implications.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: classification, feature engineering, model evaluation, interpretation.
Project 3 — Sales Forecasting
Intermediate–Advanced
Use historical sales data to forecast future demand. Compare against a simple baseline and use time-based validation rather than randomly splitting time-series observations.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: time-series analysis, forecasting, error metrics, decision support.
Project 4 — End-to-End ML Application
Advanced
Build a prediction pipeline, expose it through a small web application or API, and document the input requirements, model limitations, and testing process.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: machine learning, Python application development, deployment, reproducibility.

blocks.label: Portfolio standard
blocks.text: Each project should contain a clear problem statement, dataset source, cleaning steps, exploratory analysis, baseline, evaluation metrics, conclusions, limitations, and reproducible setup instructions. Never claim that a model is accurate or production-ready without appropriate evidence.

rows.text: Python, pandas, data visualisation, introductory machine learning

blocks.text: Start with one learning resource per subject and apply what you learn immediately. Projects and a strong grasp of fundamentals generally provide more evidence of ability than collecting many introductory certificates.

blocks.text: Potential employers include technology companies, analytics consultancies, financial services, healthcare organisations, retail businesses, research institutions, and product startups.

For a first role, do not limit yourself to the exact title Junior Data Scientist. A data analyst role with substantial SQL, Python, statistical analysis, and modelling exposure can be a useful stepping stone.
Data Science Intern / Junior Data Scientist
Data cleaning, EDA, baseline models, reporting
Data Scientist
Independent analysis, modelling, experimentation
Senior Data Scientist / Applied Scientist
Complex modelling, technical leadership, product impact
Lead Data Scientist / Data Science Manager
Strategy, team leadership, model governance, business outcomes
Alternative specialisations include machine learning engineering, applied AI, experimentation and causal inference, forecasting, risk analytics, and data engineering.
After a B.Sc in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, possible postgraduate options include:

items.text: M.Sc. in Data Science.
M.Sc. in Statistics or Applied Statistics.
M.Sc. in Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning.
M.Sc./M.Tech. in Computer Science or related computing fields, subject to eligibility.
Research-oriented postgraduate study in computational science, applied mathematics, or AI.

blocks.text: A postgraduate degree can help for research-heavy or specialised roles, but it is not universally required for entry-level industry positions. Check prerequisites carefully, particularly mathematics, statistics, programming, and any entrance examinations.

blocks.label: Generative AI and LLM applications
blocks.text: Evaluate AI outputs, analyse model behaviour, and build data-driven applications around language models.

blocks.label: Predictive analytics
blocks.text: Forecast demand, customer behaviour, equipment failures, and business outcomes.

blocks.label: Responsible AI
blocks.text: Investigate bias, fairness, data privacy, and model reliability.

blocks.label: Automated machine learning
blocks.text: Use automated workflows to accelerate experimentation while validating the results.

blocks.label: Real-time analytics
blocks.text: Analyse streaming or frequently updated data for timely decisions.

blocks.label: MLOps and model monitoring
blocks.text: Track model performance after deployment and identify data drift or degradation.

blocks.label: Decision intelligence
blocks.text: Combine statistical evidence, business context, and predictive models to support better decisions.
AI coding assistants can speed up routine tasks, but they do not remove the need to understand statistics, verify code, prevent data leakage, evaluate models correctly, and communicate uncertainty.

blocks.label: Recommended first milestone
blocks.text: Complete one end-to-end project using Python, SQL, and machine learning. For example, analyse customer churn, train and evaluate a prediction model, and explain how a business could use the results. Publish the project on GitHub with a clear README and reproducible code.
